name: Ashmark Patchlayer Thermal Liner Vest
description: A salvage-constructed quilted liner vest stitched from mismatched fabric scraps — old military surplus, transit upholstery, reclaimed insulated panels — all in muted earth tones that somehow cohere. Worn under a coat or over a shirt, it adds a full thermal zone without bulk. No brand markings; the stitching itself is the signature.
functionality: Layered salvage insulation for core warmth; no-bulk profile for under-coat or standalone wear.
what_it_says: You make do, and you've made do well enough that it almost looks deliberate.
manufacturer: Ashmark Street Construct — no fixed maker
story_hooks: One of the fabric panels is cut from a corporate uniform — the logo has been removed but the weave pattern is unmistakably Stratum Logistics.
The vest has been repaired so many times the original stitching is impossible to identify — it's effectively a different garment than it started as.
